title: Punishment for rape
plain_en: Rape is a serious, non-bailable offence. Consent obtained by force, threat, deception or when a woman cannot consent is not consent.

title: Gang rape
plain_en: When a woman is raped by one or more persons acting together, each of them is guilty of gang rape.

title: Assault or criminal force to outrage a woman's modesty
plain_en: Using force on a woman or attacking her intending to outrage her modesty (for example groping) is an offence.

title: Sexual harassment
plain_en: Unwelcome physical contact or advances, demanding sexual favours, showing pornography against your will, or making sexually coloured remarks is sexual harassment.

title: Assault with intent to disrobe
plain_en: Attacking or using force on a woman intending to disrobe her or force her to be naked is an offence.

title: Voyeurism
plain_en: Watching or capturing images of a woman in a private act, or sharing such images, is an offence, even if she agreed to the photo but not to it being shared.

title: Stalking
plain_en: Repeatedly following or contacting a woman despite her clear disinterest, or monitoring her internet, email or electronic communication, is stalking.

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult a woman's modesty
plain_en: Words, sounds, gestures or showing objects meant to insult a woman's modesty, or intruding on her privacy, is an offence.

title: Dowry death
plain_en: If a woman dies unnaturally within seven years of marriage and was harassed for dowry before her death, it is treated as dowry death.

title: Cruelty by husband or his relatives
plain_en: Physical or mental cruelty by a husband or his relatives, including harassment for dowry or property, is a criminal offence.

title: Abetment of suicide
plain_en: Driving or helping someone towards suicide is an offence.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
plain_en: Deliberately causing bodily pain or injury is an offence.

title: Acid attack
plain_en: Throwing or attempting to throw acid on a person is a grave offence. Hospitals must give free immediate treatment.

title: Extortion
plain_en: Forcing someone to hand over money or anything valuable by putting them in fear (for example threatening to leak photos) is extortion.

title: Criminal intimidation
plain_en: Threatening harm to you, your reputation, property or loved ones to make you act or stop acting is criminal intimidation.

title: Defamation
plain_en: Spreading false statements meant to harm your reputation is defamation.

title: FIR, Zero FIR and e-FIR
plain_en: You can report a cognizable offence at ANY police station regardless of where it happened (Zero FIR), and information can be given electronically. You are entitled to a free copy of the FIR.

title: Complaint to Magistrate if police refuse
plain_en: If the police refuse to register your complaint, you can approach the Superintendent of Police and then the Judicial Magistrate, who can order an investigation.

title: Statement before a Magistrate
plain_en: Your statement can be recorded by a Magistrate. In cases of sexual offences, it should be recorded by a woman Magistrate where possible.

title: Medical examination of a rape survivor
plain_en: A medical examination must be done by a registered medical practitioner, only with your consent, and the report must be prepared promptly.

title: Victim compensation
plain_en: Victims can apply to the District or State Legal Services Authority for compensation, even if the accused is not identified.

title: Free medical treatment
plain_en: All hospitals, public or private, must give free first aid and medical treatment to survivors of rape and acid attacks and inform the police.

title: Electronic evidence and certificate
plain_en: Screenshots, chats, emails and recordings can be used as evidence. They usually need a certificate describing the device and how the copy was made.

title: Identity theft
plain_en: Fraudulently using someone's password, photos-based identity or other unique identification is punishable.

title: Cheating by personation online
plain_en: Pretending to be someone else online (for example a fake profile in your name) to cheat people is punishable.

title: Violation of privacy
plain_en: Capturing, publishing or sending images of a person's private areas without consent is punishable.

title: Publishing obscene or sexually explicit material
plain_en: Publishing or sending obscene or sexually explicit material electronically, including morphed images, is punishable.

act: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
title: 24-hour takedown of intimate images
plain_en: Platforms must act within 24 hours of a complaint to remove content showing you in an intimate or sexual way, including morphed images.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Protection from domestic violence
plain_en: Physical, sexual, verbal, emotional or economic abuse at home is domestic violence. A Magistrate can grant protection orders, the right to stay in the shared home, maintenance and custody. This is a civil remedy, separate from a police case.

title: Dowry
plain_en: Giving, taking or demanding dowry is an offence.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Workplace sexual harassment (POSH)
plain_en: Workplaces with 10 or more employees must have an Internal Committee. A written complaint can be filed generally within 3 months (extendable). Others go to the district Local Committee.

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Penetrative sexual assault on a child
plain_en: Any penetrative sexual act with a person under 18 is a grave offence under POCSO, regardless of 'consent'.

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Sexual assault and harassment of a child
plain_en: Sexual touching, showing sexual content or sexual harassment of a person under 18 is punishable under POCSO.

act: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Duty to report
plain_en: Anyone who knows of sexual abuse of a child must report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit.

title: Free legal aid for women
plain_en: Every woman is entitled to free legal services (a lawyer, advice, court fees) regardless of income, through the Legal Services Authorities.
